title: Observability: Traces That Teach
objective: After this lesson you will be able to emit trace spans per agent stage, build latency/cost/quality dashboards, and alert on behavioral signals (quality drops, cost spikes, tail latency) instead of errors alone.
why: 'The bot got worse Tuesday' without traces is archaeology: no inputs, no stage timings, no way to bisect. Observability (traces with spans per node/tool/retrieval, token accounting, quality proxies, cost attribution) converts mysteries into measurements — and behavioral alerts catch the silent failures (fluent wrongness) that error rates never see.

blocks.text: Spans per stage, attributes per span

Every run emits a **trace**: spans for triage/router/nodes/tools/retrieval/generation, each with attributes (inputs hash, tokens, latency, model, verdicts, citations count). Spans nest (run → stage → call) so slow runs expand into slow stages, then slow calls. Untraced stages are unmeasurable stages — instrument at boundaries (Ch.3 handoffs make natural span edges).

blocks.caption: Span per boundary: timing, tokens, verdicts attached where work happens

blocks.text: Three dashboards, three questions. **Latency**: p50/p95/p99 per stage + tail attribution (which stage owns p99?). **Cost**: tokens per feature/tier/tenant + projection vs budget. **Quality**: gold pass rates, abstention rate, citation coverage, human-override rate, thumbs distribution. Quality dashboards need proxies (override rate ≈ correctness signal) because truth is expensive — choose proxies deliberately, document their limits.
Alert on behavior, not just errors

Error-rate paging misses silent degradation: confident wrongness has no 5xx. Behavioral alerts: abstention spikes (corpus gaps), override-rate jumps (quality drops), cost-per-task anomalies (prompt bloat/attacks), tail-latency breaches (dependency decay), refusal spikes (campaigns). Each alert names runbook + owner: paging without a runbook is noise with adrenaline.

blocks.caption: Relative-to-baseline alerts with runbooks and owners attached

blocks.title: Fire the right alert
blocks.note: Run it: expect overrideRate PAGE (0.18 > 0.15), cost quiet, p99 quiet, pages=1. Relative thresholds with baselines: quality degradation pages while normal variance stays silent.

items: Spans per stage boundary with timing/tokens/verdicts; nested traces expand slow runs into slow calls
Three dashboards (latency/cost/quality) with deliberate proxies, documented limits
Behavioral alerts (quality/cost/tail/refusal signals) with runbooks + owners; relative thresholds adapt

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice alerts and confirm only overrideRate pages. (b) Add an abstentionRate alert (2x baseline) with a corpus-gap scenario proving it fires. (c) Write the runbook stub for override-rate pages (first 3 checks in order).
hints: Baseline: override 0.18 > 0.15 PAGE; cost 0.021 < 0.04 quiet; p99 2100 < 3000 quiet. One page, correct one.
Abstention scenario: baseline 0.05, current 0.12 → fires (>0.10); runbook: corpus-gap (new content unchunked?).
Runbook: (1) sample overridden runs (what changed?), (2) check deploy log (which version introduced it?), (3) compare gold segment scores (which kind regressed?).
exercise.why: Threshold design (relative, baselined), coverage extension (new signal, proven firing), and runbook ordering (samples → versions → segments) are the three alerting judgments — each verified, with owners attached.
exercise.code: // Alert-addition pattern: signal + relative threshold + runbook + owner.

quiz.q: Answer quality drops 30% with zero 5xx change. Detection?
options: Behavioral alerts: override-rate/abstention movement pages where error rates stay silent
quiz.explain: Fluent wrongness has no status code. Quality proxies (overrides, abstention, thumbs) with relative thresholds catch silent degradation.

quiz.q: Absolute alert thresholds set once, never revisited. Fate?
options: Rot within quarters as traffic/usage grows — relative-to-baseline thresholds adapt; absolutes need constant retuning
quiz.explain: Growth moves every absolute: relative thresholds (×baseline) scale with the system. Absolutes become noise or silence.

quiz.q: Pager fires with no runbook attached. Problem?
options: Noise with adrenaline: alerts need runbooks (ordered checks) + owners, or pages produce panic instead of procedure
quiz.explain: Alerting contracts: signal + threshold + runbook + owner. Missing runbooks convert pages into improvisation.

summary: Boundary spans, three dashboards with honest proxies, behavioral alerts with runbooks. Silent failures need behavioral signals; errors alone arrive last.
next: Visible and alarmed — now the humans in the loop: sampling, queues, and reviewer UX that closes the flywheel. Next: review operations.
